CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain in the knees.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 62-year-old male who presents with bilateral knee pain that began over the weekend after moving boxes up and down basement stairs. The pain was severe enough to keep him up Saturday night. Patient reports the knees are equally painful. He has had some knee problems in the past but attributes current symptoms to repetition and weight of boxes. He has tried Tylenol and ice with minimal relief. Patient denies that the pain prevents him from activities of daily living. He reports his kidney transplant is doing well, with recent follow-up with Dr. Gutierrez a couple of weeks ago showing nothing out of the ordinary. He is compliant with his immunosuppressive medications. Hypothyroidism is well-controlled on Synthroid taken regularly, with no fatigue or weight gain. Arthritis is known to be difficult to manage due to limitations on anti-inflammatory medications secondary to kidney transplant. Patient reports occasional elbow pain but nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headaches, or other symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (for polycystic kidneys, a few years ago)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Synthroid (for hypothyroidism, taken regularly)
Immunosuppressive medications (for kidney transplant)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Good, no fever, heart rate and blood pressure fine.
Cardiac: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated on heart exam, which appears stable compared to past exams.
Knees: Right knee shows edema and erythema with pain to palpation and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears normal.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture.
White blood cell count: Not elevated.
Kidney function: Very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis in right knee: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every six hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Patient instructed to take it easy. Will consider further imaging and physical therapy referral if symptoms continue.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.
3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Will reassess in a couple of weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed given limitations on anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant status.
